prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on what you want to do. For show/nightlife convenience and one- to three-night stays, a hotel on or near the 76 Strip/Branson Landing is usually best. For outdoor/lake time, longer stays, groups or families who want space and amenities (kitchens, game rooms, hot tubs), a cabin or whole-house Airbnb near Table Rock Lake or Indian Point is usually better.

How to choose (quick pros/cons)
- Hotel (best if: short stay, want walkable access to shows/restaurants, prefer daily housekeeping, predictable check-in)
  - Pros: easy parking/check-in, onsite restaurants/pools, close to shows on 76 Country Blvd or Branson Landing, often better for solo travelers or couples.
  - Cons: less space, no kitchen, can be noisy on the Strip, extra fees for parking/meals.
- Airbnb/cabin (best if: family/group, longer stay, want kitchen/private hot tub/lake access)
  - Pros: more space, kitchen, lower per-person cost for groups, private outdoor space, better for pets.
  - Cons: cleaning/service variability, some are far from shows, extra cleaning/cancellation rules, must check parking/road access.

Best neighborhoods to target
- 76 Country Boulevard (“the Strip”): best for shows, theaters, restaurants, nightlife.
- Branson Landing / Downtown: walkable shopping, lakefront, fireworks/entertainment.
- Table Rock Lake / Indian Point / Ridgedale: lakefront cabins, boating, quiet/outdoor focus; close to Top of the Rock and Big Cedar Lodge.
- Near Silver Dollar City (Hwy 76 / Hwy 265 area): best if your main goal is the theme park.
- Hollister / Branson West: quieter, often cheaper, good access to highways and lake.

Top hotel picks (why)
- Hilton Promenade at Branson Landing — excellent location on Branson Landing, walk to shops/restaurants and water attractions.
- Chateau on the Lake — upscale lakefront resort with spa, nice if you want a pampered stay and lake views.
- Big Cedar Lodge (nearby, Ridgedale) — premier resort for outdoors, fishing, golfing, family activities; pricey but exceptional amenities.
- Radisson Hotel Branson (on 76) — centrally located on the Strip, good if you want theater access.
- Westgate Branson Woods Resort — condo-style resort good for families with kitchens and pools.
- Budget chains (Holiday Inn Express, Best Western, La Quinta) — reliable, often best value for show visitors.

Types of Airbnbs to look for (and when they’re best)
- Lakefront cabins on Table Rock Lake — best for boating, fishing, scenic relaxation.
- Cabins with game rooms & hot tubs — great for families or groups who plan to stay in evenings.
- Condos or lofts on Branson Landing — walkable to dining/entertainment; good combination of Airbnb feel + location.
- Small cottages in Hollister/Indian Point — quieter, often better value.

Practical booking tips
- Book early for summer and holiday weekends — Branson fills quickly.
- Filter for “Entire place,” check number of beds and parking, read recent reviews (last 6 months).
- Watch cleaning fees and cancellation policies — a cheap nightly rate can be offset by high fees.
- If attending shows, pick a place within a short drive to your theater (traffic around showtimes can be slow).
- If you’ll rent a boat, prioritize lake access or a nearby marina.
- For pets, confirm pet policy and yard/fencing.

If you tell me: travel dates, how many people, budget, and what you plan to do (shows vs lake vs Silver Dollar City), I can recommend 3–5 specific current listings (hotels and Airbnbs) that match your needs.
